---
title: "Research"
---

My research sits at the interface of cement chemistry, transport modelling and data science. The goal is to make cementitious materials both lower in carbon and more predictable over very long service lives.

## Themes

<div class="card-grid">
<div class="rcard"><i class="bi bi-recycle"></i><span class="card-title">Low-carbon cement design</span><p>Coupling GEMS thermodynamic modelling, machine learning and carbon accounting to search for greener cement recipes with multi-objective optimisation.</p></div>
<div class="rcard"><i class="bi bi-shield-check"></i><span class="card-title">Repository barriers</span><p>Degradation, diffusion and reactive transport across cement–bentonite–host-rock interfaces for radioactive-waste disposal.</p></div>
<div class="rcard"><i class="bi bi-bandaid"></i><span class="card-title">Self-healing UHPC/UHDC</span><p>Healing capacity and durability of ultra-high performance concrete under aggressive environments, sustained loads and cracking/healing cycles.</p></div>
<div class="rcard"><i class="bi bi-cpu"></i><span class="card-title">Data-driven materials modelling</span><p>Hybrid machine-learning and metaheuristic models, FEniCSx/FEM, HPC workflows and X-ray CT image analysis.</p></div>
</div>

## In the media

Our study *Machine learning-accelerated discovery of green cement recipes* was featured after a press release by the Paul Scherrer Institute, with coverage in Switzerland, Germany, Austria, Italy, the United Kingdom and the United States, including the Swiss Federal Government (admin.ch), idw and Yahoo News.
